page: Microsoft Azure E64-32ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EDSv5 series, provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include AVX-512 vector support, cryptographic instruction sets (AES, VAES, SHA-NI), 48 MB of L3 cache, and dedicated CPU allocation. Designed with a constrained vCPU-to-memory ratio, it integrates 512.0 GB of RAM alongside 2,577 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, but excludes dedicated hardware accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations position the E64-32ds_v5 in the upper tier for memory subsystems, achieving a strong PassMark memory score of 2,902.8 and 149.6 GB/sec in large-block uncached read operations. Compute metrics generally place within average bounds, reflected by a Geekbench multi-core score of 14,288.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 38,157.99. Strong performance is also observed in Geekbench image processing at 14,009.0 points. In contrast, prompt processing for large 70B parameter LLM models tests weakly at 6.43 tokens/sec due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware.

The constrained vCPU configuration offers high qualitative cost efficiency for software licensable per core that demands large memory footprints. By provisioning 512 GB of RAM across 32 vCPUs rather than the standard 64 vCPUs of the chassis, workloads lower licensing overhead while maintaining substantial memory density and local temporary disk throughput. The primary operational tradeoff is reduced multi-threaded CPU throughput relative to unconstrained 64-vCPU profiles.

Given its massive memory capacity and fast local SSD storage, the E64-32ds_v5 is suited for large relational databases, in-memory caching systems such as Redis, enterprise data warehouses, and memory-heavy analytics pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E64-32ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor with 32 vCPUs, 16 physical cores, and a 2.8 GHz clock speed. Built on the x86_64 architecture with Hyper-V virtualization, this instance provides a constrained core configuration delivering 512.0 GB of memory (16.0 GB per vCPU) and includes 2,577 GB of local SSD storage without a GPU accelerator. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong memory subsystem performance and image processing capabilities, alongside standard multi-core compute throughput. The server offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads governed by per-core software licensing requiring extensive memory. It is ideally suited for enterprise database hosting, in-memory data caches, memory-intensive ETL pipelines, and large-scale data analytics.
